The authors test whether peptide-forming chemistry is a general consequence of energetic processing rather than specific to a particular energy source.
AI.method: Films of glycine and glycine-d3 were grown in two ultrahigh-vacuum chambers and irradiated with 1–2 keV electrons. Products were characterized by infrared spectroscopy, temperature-programmed desorption (TPD), and vacuum-ultraviolet (VUV) spectroscopy. Deuterated glycine served as an isotopic tracer: condensation reactions forming peptide bonds release water, so D2O detection evidences peptide formation.
AI.result: Post-irradiation IR spectra of glycine-d3 showed evidence of D2O formation, corroborated by TPD, which revealed H2O for glycine and H2O, HDO, and D2O for glycine-d3. VUV spectra showed decomposition products including CO, CO2, and H2O. A non-volatile residue remained on the surface after heating. The product distribution resembles that from proton irradiation, indicating weak dependence on the energy source.
AI.conclusion: Electron irradiation of glycine produces reaction products similar to proton irradiation, suggesting the chemistry is not strongly dependent on the energy source. These findings support the possibility that larger organic molecules can form in a wide range of extraterrestrial environments, be incorporated into small bodies, and be delivered to planetary surfaces, potentially contributing to the emergence of life.

title: The Alma catalog of OB stars. IV. A massive star census of the Magellanic Clouds System
comment: The catalog is available for download via CDS
summary:
Context. The Magellanic Clouds System (MCS), comprising the Large and Small Magellanic Clouds (LMC and SMC) and the Magellanic Bridge (MB), offers a nearby laboratory for studying massive stars. Existing catalogs are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature.
  Aims. We identify candidate stars with initial masses of roughly 8 solar masses or more, including O- and early-B-type stars, supergiants, luminous blue variables, and Wolf-Rayet stars. We aim to improve completeness in reddened and crowded regions and recover sources missed by large surveys.
  Methods. We combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical and infrared surveys. We select candidates using color-magnitude and color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications. We check for duplicates and multiple systems, include literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts, especially in 30 Dor, and derive synthetic Gaia photometry where Gaia measurements are incomplete.
  Results. ALS IV contains 51 954 massive star candidates: 36 506 in the LMC, 15 264 in the SMC, and 184 in the MB. It provides homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and spectral classifications where available. Complementary photometry and HST observations recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selections. The sample traces the main massive-star populations and prominent star-forming regions across the MCS.
  Conclusions. ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.

AI.tldr: ALS IV is the most comprehensive catalog of massive star candidates in the Magellanic Clouds System, containing 51,954 sources selected from combined Gaia DR3, SIMBAD, HST, and optical/infrared data.
AI.motivation: Existing massive-star catalogs in the Magellanic Clouds System are limited by extinction, crowding, and incomplete cross-validation with the literature, motivating a more complete census.
AI.method: The authors combine Gaia DR3 astrometry and photometry with SIMBAD, HST, and complementary optical/infrared surveys, selecting candidates via color-magnitude/color-color diagrams, extinction tracks, Gaia astrometry and variability, and spectral classifications, while cross-matching duplicates, adding literature and HST-resolved sources without reliable Gaia counterparts (especially in 30 Dor), and deriving synthetic Gaia photometry where needed.
AI.result: ALS IV contains 51,954 massive star candidates (36,506 in the LMC, 15,264 in the SMC, 184 in the MB), with homogeneous identifiers and coordinates, multiwavelength photometry, astrometry, variability diagnostics, and available spectral classifications; complementary data recover reddened and crowded sources missed by Gaia-based selection.
AI.conclusion: ALS IV provides the most comprehensive census of massive star candidates in the MCS and serves as a reference for massive-star studies and future surveys and Gaia releases.

title: The ALMA REBELS Survey: multi-band dust continuum observations reveal heavily obscured starbursts among UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$
comment: 27 pages + appendices; 15 figures in main text; to be submitted to The Open Journal of Astrophysics
summary: Detailed studies with the Atacama Large Millimeter/submillimeter Array (ALMA) have shown that dust is widespread even in UV-luminous galaxies at $z\gtrsim6.5$. Multi-band continuum observations are critical to fully characterize these early dust reservoirs. We present a homogeneous analysis of multi-band ALMA observations from the REBELS Large Program and seven follow-up programs, targeting thirteen massive galaxies at $6.5\lesssim z\lesssim7.7$ in at least two bands, including Band 8. Through optically thin modified blackbody fitting, we infer the dust masses, temperatures, and infrared luminosities of our targets. Their dust temperatures span $T_\mathrm{dust}\approx30-70\,\mathrm{K}$, and a stack reveals an average $T_\mathrm{dust}=49_{-8}^{+11}\,\mathrm{K}$. Three sources nominally qualify as ultra-luminous infrared galaxies (ULIRGs; $L_\mathrm{IR}>10^{12}\,L_\odot$), with total star formation rates of $\mathrm{SFR}_\mathrm{UV+IR}\approx160-300\,M_\odot\,\mathrm{yr}^{-1}$, the highest of which is found in our most distant target, REBELS-18 at $z=7.67$. Their star formation is heavily obscured, with $\gtrsim90\%$ emerging in the infrared, compared to an already large average obscured fraction of $f_\mathrm{obs}=0.75\pm0.11$ for the stack. These SFRs are consistent with the reconstructed growth histories of some massive quiescent galaxies at $z\approx4-5$, suggesting that dusty yet UV-bright galaxies at $z\sim7$ are plausible progenitors of such systems. The sample moreover displays large dust-to-stellar mass ratios ($M_\mathrm{dust}/M_\star = 0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}\%$), best reproduced by models in which dust grows efficiently in the interstellar medium. This demonstrates that a dust-rich, IR-luminous, and heavily obscured galaxy population is already in place well into the Epoch of Reionization.

AI.tldr: A homogeneous multi-band ALMA analysis of 13 massive galaxies at z≈6.5–7.7 reveals warm (T_dust≈30–70 K) dust reservoirs, three ULIRG-class systems with heavily obscured star formation, and high dust-to-stellar mass ratios consistent with efficient in-situ ISM dust growth, showing an obscured, IR-luminous population already present in the Epoch of Reionization.
AI.motivation: ALMA studies show dust is widespread even in UV-luminous galaxies at z≳6.5, but single-band data cannot fully constrain early dust reservoirs. Multi-band continuum observations are needed to robustly characterize dust mass, temperature, and IR luminosity in these high-redshift systems.
AI.method: Homogeneous analysis of multi-band ALMA observations (REBELS Large Program plus seven follow-up programs) for 13 massive galaxies at 6.5≲z≲7.7, each observed in at least two bands including Band 8. Dust masses, temperatures, and IR luminosities are inferred via optically thin modified blackbody fitting, complemented by stacking analysis.
AI.result: Dust temperatures span T_dust≈30–70 K, with a stack-average T_dust=49_{-8}^{+11} K. Three sources qualify as ULIRGs (L_IR>10^12 L_⊙) with SFR_UV+IR≈160–300 M_⊙/yr (highest at REBELS-18, z=7.67) and ≳90% of star formation obscured; the stack has f_obs=0.75±0.11. Dust-to-stellar mass ratios are high (M_dust/M_⋆=0.4_{-0.2}^{+0.3}%), best explained by efficient ISM dust growth.
AI.conclusion: The derived SFRs match reconstructed growth histories of some massive quiescent galaxies at z≈4–5, suggesting dusty, UV-bright z∼7 galaxies are plausible progenitors. A dust-rich, IR-luminous, heavily obscured galaxy population was already in place well into the Epoch of Reionization.

title: MINDS: The mid-infrared spectrum of the disk, jets, and winds of DG Tau
comment: 30 pages, 28 figures, 2 tables. Accepted (22 October 2026) for publication in Astronomy and Astrophysics
summary: DG Tau is one of the best-studied young stellar objects in transition from a Class I protostar to a T Tauri star. It is no longer embedded in a dense molecular cloud, but still reveals features that are commonly seen in protostars at earlier evolutionary stages. DG Tau hosts a protoplanetary disk and two energetic jets that can be studied down to the immediate environment of the star and disk at optical, infrared, and X-ray wavelengths. We use the Medium Resolution Spectrometer of MIRI on the James Webb Space Telescope. DG Tau's mid-infrared spectrum consists of a very bright continuum with various silicate features, and lines of CO, H$_2$O, OH, H I, H$_2$, Ne$^{+}$, Ne$^{2+}$, Ar$^{+}$, Fe$^{+}$, and Ni$^{+}$. We find substantial grain growth to at least 2 $μ$m at an early evolutionary stage. Lines of H$_2$O and CO are formed at extremely high temperatures (600-2000 K). The ratio of warm to hot water is the lowest among previous observations of disks with JWST. This and a very strong continuum point toward the relevance of the strong accretion of DG Tau and consequently strong stellar UV irradiation. The pair of jets reveals a rich spectrum of emission lines from ions, in particular producing forbidden lines of [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], and [Ni II]. The forward jet shows a collimated structure as found previously, while the hitherto poorly described, receding jet is more widely dispersed on scales of several arcsec, showing a layered structure with the fastest components being the most collimated. The ionization of the jet gas cannot be reconciled with high-energy radiation from the star itself. Instead, we propose a unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model in which the previously studied X-ray jet plasma continuously cools, recombining ions until, at temperatures around $10^4$ K and below, metals at low ionization stages emit the observed ion lines.

AI.tldr: JWST/MIRI spectroscopy of the Class I–T Tauri transition object DG Tau reveals strong grain growth to ≥2 μm, very hot (600–2000 K) H2O/CO with the lowest warm-to-hot water ratio seen in disks, and forbidden jet lines consistent with a nonequilibrium ionization shock model.
AI.motivation: DG Tau sits at the Class I-to-T Tauri transition, retaining protostellar features despite no longer being embedded. Its disk and two jets can be probed down to the star–disk environment, making it an ideal laboratory to test how accretion, irradiation, grain evolution, and jet ionization behave at an early evolutionary stage.
AI.method: Medium Resolution Spectrometer (MRS) mid-infrared spectroscopy with JWST/MIRI, covering the disk continuum, silicate features, and atomic/molecular lines, and spatially resolving the forward and receding jets. Analysis of line excitation and comparison with a nonequilibrium ionization shock model.
AI.result: A very bright mid-IR continuum with silicate features; lines of CO, H2O, OH, H I, H2, Ne+, Ne2+, Ar+, Fe+, Ni+. Substantial grain growth to at least 2 μm at an early stage. H2O and CO formed at 600–2000 K, with the lowest warm-to-hot water ratio among JWST disk observations, indicating strong accretion and UV irradiation. Jets show forbidden [Ne II], [Ne III], [Ar II], [Fe II], [Ni II]; the forward jet is collimated, while the receding jet is widely dispersed over several arcsec with a layered structure, fastest components most collimated.
AI.conclusion: Jet ionization cannot be explained by stellar high-energy radiation. A unified nonequilibrium ionization shock model is proposed: the X-ray-emitting jet plasma cools and recombines, so that below ~10^4 K low-ionization metal lines produce the observed emission. Grain growth occurs early, and accretion-driven UV strongly shapes the inner disk chemistry.

title: The dust attenuation scaling relation in the TNG50 simulation
comment: 19 pages, 17 figures
summary: The infrared excess (IRX = L_IR / L_UV) of star-forming galaxies (SFGs) follows a tight scaling relation with star formation rate, gas-phase metallicity, and size up to z ~ 3, providing a key benchmark for galaxy formation models. We test whether TNG50 SFGs, post-processed with the radiative transfer code SKIRT, reproduce the universal IRX relation - linking IRX to metallicity, infrared luminosity, size, and inclination - and identify the origin of any offsets. We analyse 7280 TNG50-SFGs across 0 <= z <= 4, comparing their predicted IRX relations with observations and the EAGLE simulation. We test different dust-to-metal (DTM) ratios and dust compositions, recalibrate galaxy properties to observed scaling relations, and decompose the offsets into individual parameter contributions. TNG50-SFGs match the universal IRX relation closely at 0.5 <= z <= 1, but lie above it at z = 0 (+0.5 dex) and below it at z >= 2 (-0.25 dex). They follow a relation of the same functional form, with a shallower, metallicity-independent L_IR slope. At z ~ 0, TNG50-SFGs are ~1 dex fainter in L_IR than the local calibration sample, requiring extrapolation; at fixed stellar mass and L_IR, simulated and observed IRX agree within 0.04 dex. At z >= 2, TNG50-SFGs are less obscured than predicted, an offset largely removed by lowering their metallicities by ~0.2 dex. Varying the DTM ratio and dust type shifts the offset normalisation without resolving its redshift evolution: a redshift-dependent DTM ratio helps at high z, but not at z = 0. Resolving the low-z discrepancy requires both improved dust models and observational constraints on IR-faint galaxies.

AI.tldr: TNG50-SFGs post-processed with SKIRT reproduce the universal IRX relation form but show redshift-dependent offsets (+0.5 dex at z=0, -0.25 dex at z≥2); DTM ratio and dust composition shift normalization but not redshift evolution, while low-z mismatch requires better dust models and IR-faint observational constraints.
AI.motivation: The universal IRX relation linking infrared excess to star formation rate, metallicity, and size is a key benchmark for galaxy formation models, yet it is unclear whether cosmological simulations reproduce it and what drives any offsets.
AI.method: Analyzed 7280 TNG50 star-forming galaxies at 0≤z≤4 post-processed with the SKIRT radiative transfer code, compared predicted IRX relations to observations and EAGLE, tested varying dust-to-metal ratios and dust compositions, recalibrated galaxy properties to observed scaling relations, and decomposed offsets into individual parameter contributions.
AI.result: TNG50-SFGs match the IRX relation closely at 0.5≤z≤1 but lie +0.5 dex above at z=0 and -0.25 dex below at z≥2, following the same functional form with a shallower, metallicity-independent L_IR slope. At z~0 galaxies are ~1 dex fainter in L_IR than the calibration sample; at fixed stellar mass and L_IR, IRX agrees within 0.04 dex. At z≥2 reduced obscuration is largely removed by lowering metallicities ~0.2 dex. DTM ratio and dust type shift normalization without resolving redshift evolution.
AI.conclusion: Dust-to-metal ratio and composition variations cannot explain the redshift evolution of the IRX offset; a redshift-dependent DTM helps at high z but not at z=0. Resolving the low-z discrepancy requires improved dust models and observational constraints on IR-faint galaxies.

title: TESS discovers an eclipse of the Be star V1294 Aql (= HD 184279) by its not-so-small, low-mass companion
comment: 6 pgs, 4 figures. Accepted for publication in Astronomy & Astrophysics Letters
summary: In a single sector of observations with the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS), an eclipse-like event occurred in the Be star V1294 Aql. The reality of the eclipse is corroborated by $UBV$ photometry from the Hvar observatory. The event occurred at phase 17.97 of the linear ephemeris by Harmanec et al. (2022) for the upper conjunction of this SB1 binary (P$_{\rm orb}$ = 192.9 d). Therefore, we conclude that the Be star was eclipsed by its companion. With this elimination of the uncertainty of the orbital inclination, the mass of the secondary is 0.99 to 1.17 M$_\odot$ for masses of the primary from 14 to 18 M$_{\odot}$. The depth of the eclipse of $\sim$6.0% (0.06 mag) is incompatible with a white-dwarf (WD) nature of the companion. At the implied radius of $\sim$25% of that of the B0.5 primary, the secondary is not a bona-fide sdO/sdB star, either, but it could be still in its contraction phase. The increasing number of such stars may lend support to model calculations according to which the timescale of the contraction can be not thermal but instead is governed by the much slower removal of a residual H-rich envelope. It is also possible the companion is on the pre-main sequence in which case the two stars have not yet interacted. Two new interferometric observations were obtained near orbital quadrature but the secondary star was not detected, nor was it detected in high-resolution high-S/N echelle spectra.

AI.tldr: A TESS eclipse-like event in the Be star V1294 Aql is confirmed by UBV photometry, establishing that the Be primary is eclipsed by its companion. This removes the inclination ambiguity and pins the secondary mass to 0.99–1.17 M☉ (for 14–18 M☉ primary), while the 6% eclipse depth rules out a white dwarf and argues against a bona fide sdO/sdB companion.
AI.motivation: The SB1 binary V1294 Aql (P_orb = 192.9 d) had an unknown orbital inclination, which prevented a reliable determination of the secondary's mass and nature; the recent Harmanec et al. (2022) ephemeris made it possible to test whether an eclipse-like photometric event corresponds to the upper conjunction.
AI.method: TESS single-sector photometry revealed an eclipse-like event at phase 17.97 of the linear ephemeris, corroborated by UBV photometry from Hvar Observatory. The authors also obtained two interferometric observations near orbital quadrature and high-resolution, high-S/N echelle spectra to search for the secondary.
AI.result: The eclipse is real and occurs at upper conjunction, so the system is eclipsing and the inclination is fixed. The secondary mass is 0.99–1.17 M☉ for primary masses of 14–18 M☉. The eclipse depth of ~6.0% (0.06 mag) is incompatible with a white dwarf and, at an implied radius ~25% of the B0.5 primary, the companion is not a bona fide sdO/sdB star. The secondary was not detected in the interferometric or echelle observations.
AI.conclusion: The companion is likely still contracting (possibly with contraction governed by slow removal of a residual H-rich envelope rather than thermal timescale) or is on the pre-main sequence, meaning the stars have not yet interacted. The growing number of such systems supports models invoking non-thermal contraction timescales.

title: The Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) Survey I: Photometric Calibration of NB395 and Metallicity Estimation
comment: ApJS in Press
summary: We present the first results of the Zero Enrichment Rare Objects (ZERO) survey, a narrow-band photometric survey targeting metallicity-sensitive narrow bands using the Hyper Suprime-Cam on the Subaru Telescope. This paper outlines the scientific goals, survey strategy, current observational status, photometric calibration, and metallicity estimation. The current ZERO footprint comprises 21 pointings, covering approximately 35 deg$^2$ along the celestial equator in the NB395 band, reaching NB395 $\sim$ 24.5 mag (10$σ$) in one hour, significantly deeper than typical comparable narrow-band Ca H\&K surveys. The NB395 photometry is calibrated using corrected Gaia BP/RP spectra and the recalibrated SDSS Stripe 82 catalog, achieving a typical zero-point precision of $\sim$0.3 per cent and flat-field precision better than 1 per cent on spatial scales larger than 8$^\prime$. title: Multi-Frequency Inversion of Meridional Flows Using Wave-Simulation-Based Sensitivity Kernels: Kernels, Method and Validation On Synthetic Data
comment: 19 pages, 19 figures, submitted to ApJ
summary:
Measuring the solar meridional circulation is central to understanding how magnetic flux and angular momentum are redistributed within the Sun. While time-distance helioseismology has been a primary tool for probing these internal flows, current methods generally rely on broadband travel-time measurements that compress the frequency dependence of the wavefield into single values for each measurement geometry. This approach overlooks the fact that different temporal frequencies sample the solar interior differently, potentially limiting our ability to resolve complex, depth-dependent flow structures. In this paper, we present a framework for performing meridional circulation inversions using frequency-dependent travel-time shifts and corresponding sensitivity kernels derived directly from global-scale, 3D wave-propagation simulations.
  We analyze sensitivities for horizontal and radial flows, noting that higher temporal frequencies offer increased spatial resolution while their practical application is balanced by the lower signal--to--noise ratio of travel-time measurements at frequencies above the 3 mHz peak of solar oscillations. Using an iterative regularized least-squares solver, we demonstrate that our method successfully recovers many aspects of complex circulation models while remaining robust against the stochastic noise of realistic simulations. We consider the impact of different regularization operators on the inversions, and enforcing constraints like mass conservation to improve inversion results.

AI.tldr: The paper introduces frequency-dependent travel-time shifts and 3D simulation-derived sensitivity kernels to invert for the Sun's meridional circulation, improving resolution of depth-dependent flows compared to broadband time-distance helioseismology.
AI.motivation: Meridional circulation governs redistribution of magnetic flux and angular momentum in the Sun, but existing time-distance helioseismology relies on broadband travel times that collapse frequency dependence into single values per geometry, discarding the fact that different temporal frequencies sample different depths and thus limiting resolution of complex flow structures.
AI.method: A framework for meridional circulation inversions using frequency-dependent travel-time shifts with corresponding sensitivity kernels computed directly from global-scale 3D wave-propagation simulations. Sensitivities for horizontal and radial flows are analyzed across temporal frequencies; inversions use an iterative regularized least-squares solver, comparing regularization operators and enforcing mass-conservation constraints.
AI.result: Higher temporal frequencies yield improved spatial resolution, though offset by lower signal-to-noise ratios above the 3 mHz oscillation peak. The method recovers many features of complex circulation models and remains robust against stochastic noise in realistic simulations; choice of regularization operator and mass-conservation constraints measurably affect inversion quality.
AI.conclusion: Frequency-dependent, simulation-derived kernels provide a viable and more depth-resolving route to meridional circulation inversions, with regularization strategy and physical constraints (e.g., mass conservation) as key levers for improving recovered flow structure.

title: A Study of Three Intrinsically Luminous Long Period Interacting Eclipsing Binaries in the Galaxy and the Small Magellanic Cloud
comment: 22 pages with 7 figures
summary: The properties of the eclipsing binaries SMC004701.39-732645.8, SMC005609.41-722809.2 and PW Pup are examined using archival photometric and spectroscopic observations. These systems have orbital periods of hundreds of days, and contain highly evolved components with temperature differences of at least 1000 - 2000K. The SMC systems are among the brightest eclipsing binaries in that galaxy at visible wavelengths, and show excess thermal emission that appears to be typical for luminous K and M giants in that galaxy. A preliminary mass function for SMC004701 suggests a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.8 +/- 0.8 Msolar, whereas the PW Pup mass function indicates a minimum mass for the secondary of 3.2 +/- 0.3 Msolar. Light curve elements are examined for a range of mass ratios using observations at visible and mid-infrared (MIR) wavelengths. The results suggest that SMC004701 may prove to be a double line spectroscopic binary at visible wavelengths. However, with the possible exception of emission from a circumstellar disk, infrared observations will likely be required to detect light from the secondary in the other two systems. All three systems have likely experienced mass transfer, and had components with initial masses that correspond to B spectral types on the main sequence. The light associated with the secondary likely originates from a shell or disk that obscures a hotter central star.
